title: The pooler's silently-swallowed donation failure is guarded only by an unticked human checklist line, despite the check being mechanically provable in preview
description: BalancerPoolerV2._psmDonate failures are swallowed by try/catch, so a green index-4 mint transaction is NOT evidence that the donation leg works — the exact failure mode story-072 checklist line 1197 exists to catch. That line is a post-broadcast HUMAN step, is UNTICKED, and story-075's :verify explicitly declines to discharge it (VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:85-86 prints 'STILL A HUMAN STEP ... line 1197'). Nothing in the npm chain enforces that the human step ever happens. Meanwhile Phase 8's _probePoolerDonation performs exactly this assertion and PASSED in this audit's :dry run (BatchDonatedViaPSM=true, DonationSkipped=false, USDC stream buffer delta 2485691) — but Phase 8 is `if (isPreview)` only, so it never runs on the broadcast path. The same preview-only gating is the only thing that exercises BALANCER_ROUTER and SUSDS_IS_FIRST, which are private immutable with no getter and therefore unassertable by Phase 0 or by :verify.
impact: After a successful broadcast the operator can see a fully green :verify run while the new index-4 pooler silently fails every PSM donation — value that should reach the batch minter is skipped, and the wiring assertions cannot see it because the wiring is correct. Detection depends entirely on an unticked manual step.
evidence: side-effects.json -> events[0], externalCalls[4], leadsResolution[6]. Log: scratchpad/dry.log:282 'pooler: BatchDonatedViaPSM / DonationSkipped: true false'. Source: run() :439 `if (isPreview) _phase8_previewSmokeTests()`; VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:85-86.
recommendation: Add a `promotion-ready:verify-mint` npm key running the Phase 8 pooler probe in PREVIEW_MODE against LIVE POST-cutover state (prank OWNER, trigger one index-4 mint, require BatchDonatedViaPSM fired and DonationSkipped did not). It needs no broadcast and no signing, so it can be chained after `:verify` with the same `&&` discipline, converting checklist line 1197 from an unenforced human step into a fail-closed gate. Until that exists, tick line 1197 explicitly before disconnecting the Ledger.

title: The verifier's 'the cutover did not complete' gate cannot detect an incomplete cutover — the progress file is fully written during forge's local pass
description: The verifier guards against 'a verifier run against a file the cutover never finished writing' with `require(_isDeployed("NudgeStreamer") && _isDeployed("BatchNFTMinter"), "Progress file is missing core deployment records - the cutover did not complete. Resume it before verifying")`. Those records cannot signal dispatch completion: `_trackDeployment`/`_trackConfig` call `_writeProgressFileWithStatus("in_progress")` on EVERY step (:2161, :2169) and run() flips it to "completed" at :435 — all inside forge's single local pass, before transaction #1 is signed. On a partial broadcast the file therefore already exists, already carries all 14 addresses, and already says "completed". The gate can only distinguish 'the local pass aborted early' from 'the local pass succeeded' — a pre-broadcast condition, not the post-broadcast one it names. The verifier also never reads `deploymentStatus` at all (only scripts/patch-mainnet-addresses-promotion-ready.js:122 does).
impact: A guard introduced by the fix for run-22 M-01 reads as protection it does not provide. Practical harm is bounded: on a partial cutover the subsequent _phase7_wiringAssertions() still fails loudly against live chain state, so the outcome is a worse diagnostic message rather than a missed detection. Disclosure note: this is a NEW instance of the ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast family established in run-22, on a new contract introduced by the fix — new fingerprint, same family.
recommendation: Make the gate read something only dispatch can produce. Either (a) have the verifier require `deploymentStatus == "completed"` AND independently confirm on-chain code at the recorded NudgeStreamer/BatchNFTMinter addresses (`addr.code.length > 0`), which is the cheapest true dispatch signal; or (b) drop the misleading require and let Phase 7 be the sole authority, with a comment explaining why a pre-dispatch record check is impossible. Option (a) is preferred — it costs two staticcalls and turns the guard honest.

title: The persisted BPT baseline is protected against deletion but not against value corruption — no provenance binding on the `baselines` block
description: Story 074's rails check that `baselines.bptAtCutover` is PRESENT (:564) and NON-ZERO (:571, and again in the verifier at :151). They never check that it is the RIGHT value. There is no chainId, block-number, or run binding on the `baselines` object, and no checksum. On a resume leg the live read of the emptied old pooler is 0, so `bptAtPhase0 = max(persisted, 0) = persisted` — a baseline hand-edited downward to any smaller non-zero value is adopted verbatim, and the Phase 7 conservation assertion under-detects a shortfall by exactly the delta. The `//promotion-ready:resume` doc key's rule ('TRIM THE contracts BLOCK ONLY, NEVER the top-level baselines block') is enforced for deletion by two independent aborts, but is documentation-only for the value.
impact: Weakens, without defeating, the conservation assertion story-074 exists to make non-vacuous. NOTE: this does NOT trigger story-074's stated conditional-Medium ('weakening any rail re-classifies L-02 as Medium') — no existing rail is weakened, and one was tightened; this is an uncovered residual, not a regression. Plausibility is low: it requires digit-editing the value, not the trimming slip the runbook warns about. Filed for recall, not because it is likely.
evidence: side-effects.json -> fixVerification.run22_L02.adversarialProbes (the two `covered: false` / `partial` entries). Source: :2013-2020, :549, :564, :571; VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:147-154.
recommendation: Emit a sibling `baselines.bptAtCutoverBlock` (decimal string, written at the same time as the value) and have both Phase 0 and the verifier require it is non-zero and `<= block.number`, plus log the pair prominently so a corrupted value is visible. Cheaper alternative: log `baselines.bptAtCutover` in human units at the top of every leg and require the operator confirm it against the `:dry` run's Phase 0 'stranded value (live)' block.

title: The verifier's read-only guarantee is structural but its guards do not pin it: a misnamed flag check plus a substring-only guard test over an inherited mutating surface
description: Two compounding weaknesses in the verifier's safety story. (1) `_requireNoBroadcastFlag()` is named for a check it cannot perform — it only rejects PREVIEW_MODE (:97); its own NatSpec admits no cheatcode reports --broadcast. (2) `VerifyPromotionReady is DeployMainnetPromotionReady is Script, StdCheats`, so the compiled artifact retains StdCheats and the read-write `./server/deployments` fs_permissions grant, while test/VerifyPromotionReadyGuards.t.sol pins read-only-ness with raw substring scans for cheatcode LITERALS only ('startBroadcast','startPrank','vm.deal','vm.warp','forge-std/Test.sol','OLD_POOLER'). A future edit calling an inherited mutating helper — `_writeProgressFileWithStatus(...)` is the obvious one — would pass every current assertion, as would a live-read BPT fallback written through a local variable or a differently-named constant instead of the literal OLD_POOLER.
impact: LATENT ONLY — graded honestly. No current code path reaches a mutating helper: the verifier's full call graph is run -> _requireNoBroadcastFlag / _loadAndValidateProgressFile / _adoptPersistedBptBaseline / _phase7_wiringAssertions / _verifyMintAuthorityInvariance / _printSummary, all view or storage-only, and the standalone run empirically mutated nothing (trace shows only vm.envOr plus a failed vm.readFile before aborting). A :verify run mistakenly given --broadcast is inert because no broadcast context is ever opened. The risk is regression on a future edit, plus a maintainer trusting the function name.
evidence: side-effects.json -> verifyLegStandalone, testHarnessAssessment, leadsResolution[0] and [1]. Source: VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:89-98; test/VerifyPromotionReadyGuards.t.sol:114-133; foundry.toml fs_permissions read-write ./server/deployments.
recommendation: Rename `_requireNoBroadcastFlag` to `_requireNoPreviewMode` so the name matches the check, and keep the NatSpec paragraph explaining why the broadcast flag is unobservable. Strengthen the guard test from substring scanning to a call-graph assertion: assert the verifier's source contains no call to any of the inherited mutating helpers by name (`_writeProgressFileWithStatus`, `_trackDeployment`, `_trackConfig`, `_phase1_`..`_phase6_`, `_phase4d_`, `_phase8_`, `_moveBPT`, `_rescueTo`, `_migrateStaker`, `_collectNudgeFromOwner`, `_swapUniboost`), and assert the presence of `bptAtCutoverPersisted` rather than only the boolean flag. Best structural fix: split the shared constants and read-only helpers into a base contract that neither the verifier nor the cutover inherits mutating code from, so the verifier cannot inherit a broadcast surface at all.

title: The post-broadcast human checklist quotes stale expected figures, degrading the one control story-075 deliberately does not discharge
description: story-072 checklist line 1195 — one of only two unticked items and, alongside line 1197, the entire compensating human control — instructs the operator to confirm 'the new pooler holds the full 16,338.8190 BPT' and 'the rescued ~349 USDC sits in the streamer buffer'. Both figures are stale. This audit's live :dry run measured 16,867.5264 BPT (16867526417628291567945 wei) and a final stream buffer of 530.761796 USDC (99.224124 from the old batch minter + 51.537672 UniboostSCX residual prime + 380.000000 from DelayRelease). The CODE is unaffected — Phase 0 derives the baseline live (side-effects.json confirms bptAtPhase0 == the live figure) and no assertion references the stale number; the 16,338.819e18 literal survives only as a self-contained fixture in test/BptBaselinePersistence.t.sol:96. The defect is confined to the manual control.
impact: Law-3 owner footgun: non-obvious, and a competent non-malicious operator would be surprised. Every quoted figure will mismatch at cutover time, so the operator either aborts a healthy cutover on a false alarm, or — the dangerous direction — learns that the checklist numbers are 'always a bit off' and waves through a genuine BPT shortfall. Because line 1195 is precisely what story-075 leans on for anything :verify cannot mechanise, degrading it degrades the whole compensating-control story.
evidence: side-effects.json -> leadsResolution[3], preconditionResults (bptAtPhase0 = 16867526417628291567945), stateWrites (USDC breakdown 99224124 + 51537672 + 380000000 = 530761796). Log: scratchpad/dry.log:117-124, :156, :184-185, :199.
recommendation: Stop hardcoding balances in the human checklist. Rewrite line 1195 to say 'confirm the new pooler's BPT equals the `BPT cutover baseline` printed by Phase 0 of the immediately preceding `:dry` run, and the streamer buffer equals its final `collectNudge -> stream buffer now` figure' — the script already prints both, under a '--- stranded value (live) ---' header built for exactly this purpose. Additionally have `_printSummary()` emit a copy-paste 'POST-BROADCAST HUMAN CHECKLIST' block with the live-derived expected values filled in, so the operator compares against measurements rather than against prose written weeks earlier.

title: Phase 6 consumes the snapshot's user list without ever checking the snapshot targeted the same staker addresses the script will migrate
description: `_loadSnapshotUsers` reads only `.stakers.<key>.users` from scripts/snapshots/depletion-stakers-latest.json. The snapshot file DOES record `.stakers.<key>.address` (verified: all three currently equal V1_STAKER_EYE/SCX/FLX exactly), but the script never cross-checks it against its own constants, never checks the file's `blockNumber` for staleness, and never checks the file exists at all before Phases 1-5 are queued. Upstream, scripts/snapshot-depletion-stakers.js:98-106 resolves those addresses by regex over server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts — the stale-trap pattern already recorded for this project, where that file has previously carried 0x000…0 'not deployed' placeholders for LIVE funded contracts; the regex `(0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40})` accepts a zero placeholder as a valid match. RECONCILIATION: this is the same missing-Phase-0-probe root cause as run-22 L-07 (b28492ce…) and should be collapsed into it by the deduplicator; the address-provenance and staleness dimensions are the increment L-07 did not cover.
impact: Fail-CLOSED but LATE, which is the whole cost. A wrong or incomplete user list is caught by `require(old.totalStaked() == 0, "V1 still holds stake after migrate - widen the snapshot and re-run")` (:1681) and the conservation assert (:1682) — so there is no silent bad migration. But those fire inside Phase 6, after Phases 1-5 have already been dispatched on a one-shot hardware-signed mainnet run, leaving a partially-applied cutover that must be recovered through the hand-trimming resume runbook. A missing snapshot file is worse still: vm.readFile reverts with a raw filesystem error rather than an actionable message.
evidence: side-effects.json -> leadsResolution[4] and [5]. Snapshot JSON inspected: all three `.address` fields match the script constants at :182-184. Source: :1599-1601, :1681-1682; scripts/snapshot-depletion-stakers.js:98-106.
recommendation: Add a Phase 0 snapshot probe that runs before any mutation: vm.readFile(SNAPSHOT_FILE) inside a try/catch with an actionable revert ('run `npm run promotion-ready:snapshot` first'); then require `.stakers.<key>.address == V1_STAKER_<X>` for all three; require `.chainId == 1`; and require `.blockNumber` is within a freshness window of `block.number` so a stale user list cannot be silently reused (the .gitignore comment at :15 already states stale lists 'must never be committed or silently reused' — this makes that rule structural). Separately, harden resolveAddress() to reject the zero address explicitly rather than accepting it as a valid 40-hex match.
